01How it works

Start to finish.

  1. You text me your business name.

    That's all I need. If you already have a website, I'll look at what's hurting it, usually how it loads and reads on a phone.

  2. I build your new site.

    The real thing, with your services, your area and your phone number on it. Not a mockup, not a template with your logo dropped in.

  3. You open it on your phone.

    That's where your customers will see it, so that's where you should judge it. Tap around. Show your spouse. Take your time.

  4. You decide.

    If you want it, I put it live on your own domain in 5 business days. If you don't, that's the end of it.

If you don't like it, you don't pay, and you keep the page anyway.

02The work

Every business gets its own design.

These are the actual pages, scrolling inside a phone. A barber's price board, a photographer's prints on a table, a landscaper's property plan. Nothing here started from a template.

Barber

Norfolk, Virginia. Built from his Booksy profile.

Black, gold and dark green, the way he asked. His whole menu on a board, and every cut books straight into his calendar.

Photographer

Portraits, weddings, real estate and aerial. Built from their own site and photographs.

Their photographs laid out as prints on a table, their rates as index cards. Sixteen of their own pictures, none of ours.

Landscaping and hardscaping crew

Delaware. Concept build.

All fifteen of their services drawn onto one property plan. Tap a number and the plan shows you where that job happens.

Hot tub and pool service

Omaha, Nebraska. Concept build.

Customers tap the services they want, a bar adds them up, and the whole request goes to the owner as one text. No monthly booking fee.

Plumber

San Diego. Demo with sample details.

Built for the person with water on the floor. The call button is within reach of a thumb on every screen.

You never get a sales deck from me. Just a link.

Then it's your call.
